headline: US stocks ended mixed as a chip and AI selloff offset relief from falling oil prices and easing Middle East tensions ahead of next week’s major tech earnings
raw_text:
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose while the S&P 500 was flat and the Nasdaq Composite and Russell 2000 declined, as weakness in chip and AI names countered support from lower oil and reduced geopolitical tension.
- Concerns about soaring AI-related capital spending and potential credit risks for Amazon (AMZN), Meta (META), and Alphabet (GOOGL) persisted after Moody’s warnings and nearly $800 billion in prior-day market cap losses for the Magnificent Seven.
- Intel (INTC) fell sharply despite reporting strong Q2 results, upbeat guidance, and AI-driven server CPU strength, while other semiconductors including AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), Marvell (MRVL), and Micron (MU) also declined, making technology the session’s clear laggard.
- Tesla (TSLA) extended its recent slide, falling again after posting record Q2 deliveries but with compressed margins amid surging CapEx and AI investments.
- Tenet Healthcare (THC) jumped after strong Q2 results that featured a 16% increase in adjusted EBITDA and raised 2026 guidance.
- Safety Insurance Group (SAFT) surged more than 41% during the session.
- RingCentral (RNG) climbed about 25% after beating fiscal Q2 estimates, raising its 2026 outlook, and hiking its dividend.
- MaxLinear (MXL) dropped more than 21% and Hims & Hers Health (HIMS) fell 13%, ranking among the day’s notable decliners.
- Industrials, financials, healthcare, and other defensive sectors outperformed, aided by lower oil prices and easing inflation and geopolitical concerns, while semiconductors and broader tech lagged.
- After-hours trading was muted with no major earnings-related moves over roughly 2%, only modest activity in names such as Digital Realty (DLR), as investors looked ahead to next week’s reports from Meta (META), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Apple (AAPL) alongside further geopolitical updates.
